skill.name: homepage-to-profile
skill.description: Uses Leadsets to turn public company homepages into profiles of products, audiences, positioning, named customers, and key links. It checks available scrape units and tests one domain before processing a batch.
skill.summary: Build company research profiles from public homepages with Leadsets.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The shell execution and system reconnaissance alerts are false positives. The Leadsets endpoint is used to process submitted domains; the other flagged URLs are reference links. No embedded prompt injection or credential exfiltration was found, but the instructions leave gaps in handling scraped content and enforcing spending limits.

remediation.issue: Submitted domains are shared with Leadsets.
remediation.suggestion: Name Leadsets during the pre-run confirmation and obtain approval before submitting the domain list, especially when it contains confidential account selections.

remediation.issue: Scraped text is not explicitly treated as untrusted.
remediation.suggestion: Use scraped text only as source data. Ignore instructions from pages and keep tool actions within the original request and approved destination.

remediation.issue: Untrusted fields can be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas.
remediation.suggestion: Write scraped fields as literal text in Sheets and neutralize formula interpretation in CSV exports. Test both paths with formula-like values.

remediation.issue: Batches can spend units before their actual cost is checked.
remediation.suggestion: Use an enforceable per-call cap if available. Otherwise, check the documented maximum cost before each call and stop when it cannot fit.

semantic_findings.title: Scraped Pages Are Not Explicitly Treated as Untrusted
semantic_findings.description: The workflow turns public site content into profiles and can write them to an external destination. It does not tell the agent to ignore instructions embedded in retrieved pages.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The steps use retrieved content to assemble records before a write. No instruction in the skill separates page content from trusted directions.

semantic_findings.title: Scraped Fields Lack Spreadsheet Formula Protection
semantic_findings.description: Public site text is exported to CSV or Google Sheets without instructions to preserve it as literal text. Spreadsheet software could interpret a crafted field as a formula.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The export of externally controlled fields is explicit, but the connector's treatment of cell values is not specified.

semantic_findings.title: Scrape Budget Is Checked After Batch Spending
semantic_findings.description: The initial estimate uses one domain, and actual usage is checked after each later batch. A more expensive batch can exceed the requested limit before the next check.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The steps require an estimate and an after-batch check. They do not specify a per-call cap or a worst-case check before each batch.

content.value_statement: Company websites describe products, audiences, and customers in different ways. Turn public homepage content into consistent profiles for comparing companies.
actual_capabilities: Accepts domains or full URLs from a pasted list, CSV, or Google Sheet column.
Normalizes inputs to homepages and removes duplicates.
Checks available scrape units and uses one domain to estimate batch costs.
Extracts products, stated audiences, positioning, named customers, and key links when present.
Returns short profiles in chat or exports a table to CSV or a connected Google Sheet.
Reports domains with no usable data, pages read, and scrape units used.
limitations: Scraping requires paid Leadsets scrape units and is not available on the free plan.
Only public pages covered by the scraper are available. It cannot read pages behind a login or paywall.
It does not find people or email addresses, or infer missing details such as headcount or industry.
The first scrape is billable, and its cost only estimates the cost of later domains.

use_cases.title: Prepare for a Sales Conversation
use_cases.description: Review a prospect's products, stated audience, and named customers before a call.

use_cases.title: Compare Competitor Positioning
use_cases.description: Compare how selected competitors describe their products and audiences, using only their public website claims.

use_cases.title: Document Companies in a CRM
use_cases.description: Turn a CRM domain export into a table of stated products and audiences, with unavailable sites flagged for follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: Profile One Company
prompt_templates.prompt: Profile [company domain]. Tell me what it sells and who it says it sells to. Return the result in chat.

prompt_templates.title: Check Named Customers
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: Keep only public customer evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: For these two domains, list only customers explicitly named on the site. Include case study links when available. Flag missing names and links.

prompt_templates.title: Export Profiles From a CSV
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Standardize a list for spreadsheet review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Profile the domains in the Domain column of my CSV. Remove duplicates and export products, audience, positioning, and key links. List unavailable domains separately.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Budgeted Batch
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Control paid usage and confirm the export destination.
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm the Leadsets transfer and my Google Sheet before starting. Check available units and estimate the batch after one approved probe. Ask before continuing if the estimate exceeds 40 units or the remaining balance. Report usage and domains with no usable data.

output_examples.input: Profile one company in chat and show only details supported by its homepage.
output: Key links: Pricing and product documentation.
Usage: Two pages read and two scrape units used.

output_examples.input: Profile eight domains from my spreadsheet and export the results as a CSV.
output: Seven unique domains after removing one duplicate.
One domain had no usable data because the site was unreachable.

best_practices: Confirm which domains may be shared with Leadsets and where the results may be written.
Set a unit budget and review the first paid scrape before approving a large batch.
Keep missing fields visible and check source links before relying on customer claims.
anti_patterns: Submit a confidential account list without permission to share it with Leadsets.
Treat a homepage claim as independent proof of a current customer relationship.
Import untrusted scraped values into a spreadsheet without checking that they remain plain text.

faq.question: What do I need to run this skill?
faq.answer: You need a Leadsets account with paid scrape units and either a connected Leadsets MCP server or a Leadsets API key for REST access.

faq.question: Does the first test scrape use units?
faq.answer: Yes. Checking the balance is free, but the test scrape uses units for the pages it reads.

faq.question: Can I submit a full website URL?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill normalizes full URLs to company homepages, so it does not target a specific page path.

faq.question: What happens when a homepage is blocked or unreachable?
faq.answer: The skill marks the domain as having no usable data and reports the reason when known.

faq.question: Can this find named customers and contact emails?
faq.answer: It can list customers explicitly named on public pages. It does not collect contact details or verify email addresses.

faq.question: Where can I receive the results?
faq.answer: You can receive short profiles in chat, a CSV export, or a Google Sheet when your agent has a connected Sheets integration.
